description: A sophomore Data Science major who is highly confident in discrete mathematics and logic but feels intimidated by the transition from Python to low-level memory management in C++.

nodes.personalizationRationale: Because this student has no_prior_exposure to C++, this scaffolding node ensures they understand basic syntax before moving to complex memory management.
nodes.title: C++ Syntax Foundations for Python/Java Programmers
nodes.description: Introduction to C++ syntax, primitive types, and control structures for students coming from high-level languages like Python or Java.
In-depth look at memory addresses, the pointer operator (*), and the reference operator (&) within the C++ memory model.
nodes.title: Understanding Pointers and References
nodes.personalizationRationale: Since the student reports no_prior_exposure to C++, additional scaffolding on pointers and references is required to build the foundational knowledge for data structure implementations.

nodes.title: Manual Memory Management & Lifecycles
nodes.description: Practical application of dynamic memory allocation using 'new' and 'delete' and understanding the object lifecycle/destructors.
nodes.personalizationRationale: A student with no_prior_exposure to C++ needs specific scaffolding on manual memory management to avoid memory leaks in future assignments.
This core node covers the required block_01 material on OO design and templates essential for all students.
nodes.description: C++ Object-Oriented Design: Inheritance, polymorphism, and the syntax for C++ templates for generic programming.
nodes.title: C++ Classes, Inheritance, and Templates
Exceptions and Robust Software Design
nodes.description: Designing robust programs using C++ exception handling and understanding the Goodrich/Tamassia design philosophy.
nodes.personalizationRationale: This core node completes the block_01 requirement for exception handling and design patterns.
This core node satisfies the block_02 requirement covering the implementation of fundamental linear structures.
nodes.title: Linked Lists & Recursive Logic
nodes.description: Implementation of Singly, Doubly, and Circularly Linked Lists and the principles of Recursion.
Formal assessment of recursion concepts and asymptotic analysis (Big-O notation) as applied to arrays and lists.
nodes.title: Quiz 1: Recursion & Big-O Analysis
nodes.personalizationRationale: This assessment node serves as Quiz 1, testing core recursion and Big-O competencies required for block_02.

nodes.title: Stacks, Queues, and Deques
nodes.description: The Stack and Queue Abstract Data Types (ADTs) and their implementation using arrays and linked lists.
nodes.personalizationRationale: This core node fulfills the block_03 requirement for sequence-based data structures.
Core coverage of vectors and iterators is mandatory for understanding modern C++ data access patterns in block_03.
nodes.title: Vectors, Lists, and Iterators
nodes.description: Dynamic arrays (Vectors), the Iterator pattern, and their roles in the C++ Standard Template Library (STL).

nodes.personalizationRationale: Bubble sort provides the initial framework for sequence sorting required in block_03.
nodes.title: Sequences & Bubble Sort Analysis
nodes.description: Analysis and implementation of Bubble Sort and the general concept of sequence sorting.

nodes.personalizationRationale: This assessment node serves the required midterm-review function for material covered through block_03.
nodes.description: Comprehensive review of all material from C++ foundations through sequence structures in preparation for the midterm exam.
nodes.title: Midterm Review Assessment Checkpoint

nodes.personalizationRationale: This node fulfills the block_04 requirement for introducing non-linear tree structures.
nodes.description: General tree structures, terminology (root, leaf, height), and implementation strategies.
nodes.title: General Trees and Binary Trees
Tree Traversal Algorithms
nodes.description: Standard traversal algorithms: Pre-order, Post-order, and In-order traversals for binary and general trees.
nodes.personalizationRationale: Traversal logic is a core requirement of block_04 that builds upon basic tree knowledge.

nodes.description: Priority Queue ADT and its efficient implementation using a Heap (Binary Heap) structure.
nodes.title: Priority Queues & Heaps
nodes.personalizationRationale: This node covers the essential block_05 content for priority queues and heap properties.
Hash tables and maps are critical block_06 topics required for all students to master dictionary-style lookups.
nodes.title: Maps, Hash Tables, and Skip Lists
nodes.description: Implementation of Maps and Hash Tables, focusing on hash functions, collision resolution, and skip lists.

nodes.personalizationRationale: BST and AVL trees are foundational components of the theory-heavy block_07 syllabus.
nodes.title: Binary Search Trees & AVL Trees Balancing
nodes.description: Binary Search Trees (BST) and the necessity of balancing, featuring AVL tree rotations.

nodes.personalizationRationale: This node completes the block_07 requirement for advanced balanced search structures.
nodes.title: Red-Black & Multi-Way Search Trees
nodes.description: Comparison of Multi-way search trees, (2,4) trees, and Red-Black trees implementation and proofs.

nodes.title: Advanced Sorting: Merge Sort & Selection Sort
nodes.description: Detailed analysis of Merge Sort, Selection Sort, and their comparative performance in various scenarios.
nodes.personalizationRationale: Sorting algorithms form the core of the final block_08 capstone material.

nodes.title: Cumulative Final Course Review
nodes.description: Cumulative review of the entire syllabus, including data structure selection, Big-O analysis, and C++ best practices.
nodes.personalizationRationale: This mandatory assessment node in block_08 prepares the student for the cumulative final examination.
